Documentation / Developer / Document typography and font licensing

Document typography and font licensing

Perastage resolves the requested family, weight and style to the exact approved font bytes before composition. FontCatalog owns immutable resource data, version, PostScript face name, OFL provenance and SHA-256. Rendering targets use the resolved fingerprint and glyph ID. Persisted styles keep the family and variant authored by the user, so substituting a face does not change the project.

Approved resources

PerastageSans is the application name for the original Noto Sans face. It is the default family. PerastageSans, Noto Serif and Source Sans 3 offer Regular, Bold, Italic and Bold Italic. Noto Sans Mono offers Regular and Bold. Noto Sans Arabic and Noto Sans Hebrew supply upright Regular and Bold script fallback. Third-party notices identify the exact releases, files and licenses. Only these SHA-256 identities enter the catalog. The files are static single-face TrueType fonts with unrestricted embedding flags. An unrestricted OS/2.fsType on its own gives no license evidence.

The immutable catalog checks packaged resources during application initialization. Missing or unusable resources trigger targeted filename probes in the platform font roots, then a bounded walk of 8,192 entries and six directory levels. Candidates are filtered by file size before format, embedding and SHA-256 validation. A match may have a different filename. The roots cover Windows Fonts and per-user Microsoft Fonts, macOS system, local and user Fonts, and Linux standard, XDG and user font directories. Custom platform registration paths outside these directories are outside this discovery scope. Discovery results stay cached until an explicit refresh or a project reopens with an incomplete catalog. Perastage does not install fonts or attach them to projects.

CFF, collections, web fonts and variable fonts are unsupported. Additions need a verified provenance and rights record, pinned bytes, a supported outline and cmap check, exact installed-package files and the upstream license text. The application uses the same package contract on Windows, Linux and macOS.

Composition and adapters

HarfBuzz applies OpenType shaping, kerning, positioning and ligatures. ICU computes grapheme boundaries, line opportunities and visual bidi runs, with paragraph embedding levels retained across wrapping. The renderer receives stable face fingerprints, glyph IDs, UTF-8 cluster ranges, positions, offsets, advances and baselines in scene metres or document points. Font selection checks whole graphemes before shaping and groups adjacent graphemes with the same face, direction, script and style. Unicode source is preserved as authored. HarfBuzz handles canonical equivalents such as precomposed and decomposed accents during shaping. FreeType reads the validated font bytes for simple, composite and transformed contours, including quadratic and cubic curves. A malformed outline uses the approved face's missing-glyph contour and records a diagnostic.

The approved repertoire covers Western European text, Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic and Hebrew where the selected or fallback face supplies the required glyphs. Full CJK and emoji coverage are outside the bundled repertoire. Unsupported clusters retain their source and use a missing-glyph contour where available. Script fallback uses real upright Arabic and Hebrew faces even when the surrounding text requests italic.

Fixture Label Editor drafts, source 2D labels and Layout capture share their existing field composition. The default face preserves the established NanoVG halo and the shared positions. Other approved faces use their glyph contours. Layout replay renders the captured contours with the stored physical outline widths. Raster antialiasing and the zoom-independent 2D halo policy may differ from paper ink.

Free text uses the same point-space text block plan for Layout and PDF. Rich text remains serialized in its original wx XML model. Extraction preserves families, weights, sizes, italic requests, foreground colors, underlines, strikethrough, explicit breaks, paragraph alignment, spacing and indentation. Approved family selections enable word wrapping. Existing text without an explicit approved family retains explicit line breaks and clipping. Legacy native-font metrics could vary by platform. Default sizing now uses the shipped faces, so historical free-text widths can change. Non-text rich objects and uncommon XML style features remain in the source XML with limited rendering support. The Document preview button renders the current edits with the shared point-space composition. The native editor registers approved faces where wxWidgets supports it. Native rendering and caret geometry can vary by platform. Opening and accepting the dialog without editing text keeps the original rich-text XML. Native editing can rewrite XML that wxWidgets does not round-trip.

Legend and Event Table retain their shared point-space composition and size formulas from the integration branch. The older split-export PDF compensation had already been replaced there. Fixture names retain their historical two-space-delimited-word breaks. Viewport capture and Layout raster archives invalidate incompatible plans. The existing per-viewport label cache and bounded shared outline cache avoid repeating glyph work.

PDF output and persistence

The exporter uses Type 0 fonts with TrueType CIDFont descendants, an explicit CID-to-glyph map and a ToUnicode CMap. CIDs encode glyph IDs and the original UTF-16 sequence, including surrogate pairs and ligature source. A multi-glyph cluster uses a PDF ActualText span around its selectable glyphs. The PDF places glyphs at the composed positions. It draws fixture outlines as vector paths and leaves the glyph fill selectable. Only used approved faces are embedded. Missing faces and unsupported glyphs are recorded once per issue in the export report. Font resource failure leaves scene contents and requested style values intact.

Label presentation version 3 adds the optional fontFamily field. Layout's presentation wrapper reads both versions 2 and 3. Unchanged label styles continue to write version 2. Legends and Event Tables have an optional fontFamily property in the existing Layout schema and use the default when the field is absent. Free text retains its existing per-run rich-text data. PSTG and templates store presentation choices without introducing font data into MVR or GDTF. Reopening a project revalidates an incomplete catalog, allowing restored packaged or installed resources to recover the requested appearance. The Layout text editor's Refresh fonts action also rechecks a complete catalog. Resource fingerprints invalidate the relevant capture and composition caches.

Verification

PdfFontMetricsEncoding covers catalog authorization, exact installed-face recovery, actual glyph identity, fallback, advances and mixed-family runs. LayoutLicensedFontsPdf uses Poppler to validate a representative Layout's faces, logical Unicode extraction in both default and raw mode, and outline/selection behavior. Official Windows, Linux and macOS CI require Poppler. A local configuration without Poppler reports the missing validation tools and still runs the structural test. Layout preview and PDF tests compare geometry in document points. The raster parity tests compare ink geometry with tolerances for antialiasing and rasterizer differences.

HarfBuzz, FreeType and ICU are required CMake dependencies and are resolved from the pinned vcpkg manifest for official builds. ICU supplies Unicode segmentation and bidi through its C API. See the third-party notices for their licenses and transitive package notices.
